title: Incentive Reserve Rate after Fraud Disqualifications and Bonus Clawbacks (Driver Earnings and Wayfare Pro)
content:
The incentive reserve kept back from a hold-release payout on a **Driver Earnings and Wayfare Pro** earnings account is the reserve base multiplied by the reserve rate. The reserve rate follows how many trip disqualifications for fraud (debits taking back a trip's pay with the reason fraudulent trip) and bonus clawbacks were posted to the account within the reserve lookback, the last 3 whole months back from the day the hold is lifted, the two kinds of entry counted together:

1. 2 or more of them set the reserve rate at 1.0, the whole reserve base;
2. at least one but fewer than 2, that is exactly 1, sets it at 0.5, half the reserve base;
3. none sets it at zero.

Counts are taken from the earnings statement as it stands when the hold is lifted.

## Rate schedule

| Fraud disqualifications and bonus clawbacks together, last 3 whole months | Reserve rate |
|---|---|
| 0 | 0 |
| 1 | 0.5 (50%) |
| 2 | 1.0 (100%) |
| 3 or more | 1.0 (100%) |

## Basis questions answered

**Are the two kinds of entry counted separately?** No. One fraud disqualification and one bonus clawback in the 3 months make 2 together, which sets the rate at 1.0.

**Does any other debit count?** No. Only debits with the reason fraudulent trip, and bonus clawbacks, enter the count; a route-inefficiency clawback or a fee reversal does not.

**Hypothetical figure.** A reserve base of 80.00 with exactly 1 fraud disqualification in the 3 months gives 40.00 as the reserve base multiplied by the reserve rate (80.00 multiplied by 0.5); with none, that product is 0.00.
